newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean supermarket sales up 21 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: Chilean supermarket sales up 21 pct in August.

text.p: Chilean supermarket sales in August rose 20.7 percent in real terms compared with the same month of 1995, the National Statistics Institute (INE) said Monday.
Supermarket sales rose 6.7 percent from the previous month.
Although supermarket sales have been rising rapidly, August's rate was much greater than usual. The INE report gave no explanation for the higher rate .
In nominal terms, sales rose 27 percent in August from the same month last year, and 7.8 percent from the previous month.
For the first eight months of the year, supermarket sales climbed 13.2 percent in real terms over the same period last year and 21.6 percent in nominal terms.
Supermarket sales are watched as an indicator of overall consumer spending.
A total of 549 stores, 160 of them in Santiago, are used to compile the sales figures, it said.
